title: What's this? A wardrobe is a "she"
goal: Ask what things are called, say what they're not, and understand why every Ukrainian noun has a gender — plus how to guess it from the end of the word, almost always without a dictionary.
bekal: ask and say the names of things
guess a noun's gender from its ending
tell це apart from цей / ця / це

dialogs.title: Діалог — The new rented room
dialogs.intro: Ani has just moved into a rented room. Oksana shows her in and points at things one by one. Notice that Ani doesn't ask what the words mean — she asks what gender they are, and that's exactly the right question.

lines.speaker: Оксана:
lines.id: This is a window. And this is a door.

lines.speaker: Ані:
lines.id: And what's this? Is it a table?

lines.speaker: Оксана:
lines.id: No, it's not a table. It's a wardrobe.
lines.literal: no, this — not — table. this — wardrobe.

lines.speaker: Ані:
lines.id: Wardrobe... Is it a "he" or a "she"?

lines.speaker: Оксана:
lines.id: A wardrobe is a "she". A table is a "he".

lines.speaker: Оксана:
lines.id: Because шафа ends in -a. All words ending in -a are feminine.
lines.literal: because — wardrobe — ends — on -a. all — words — on -a — feminine — gender (of).

lines.speaker: Оксана:
lines.id: A window is an "it". Neuter gender.

lines.speaker: Оксана:
lines.id: You're welcome. It's easy, isn't it?

notes: **Every noun has one of three genders, no exceptions.** It has nothing to do with being alive: *шафа* (wardrobe) is feminine, *стіл* (table) masculine, *вікно* (window) neuter. Gender says nothing about the thing itself — it only decides the endings of the adjectives and verbs that attach to it later.

**The good news: the ending almost always tells you.** Ends in **-а** or **-я** → feminine. Ends in a **consonant** → masculine. Ends in **-о** or **-е** → neuter. Those three rules cover about nine out of ten words you'll meet at A1.
**Двері is always plural.** Like English "scissors" or "trousers", *двері* (door) has no singular — even a single door is *двері*. Adjectives attached to it are plural too: *нові двері* (a new door).

**Чи means "or" in questions.** *Він чи вона?* — he or she? For "or" in ordinary statements people use **або**: *кава або чай* (coffee or tea). In everyday speech the two often swap places without any problem.

**Тому що = because.** Two words, always together. Don't split them. To ask for the reason, say **Чому?** (*cho-MOO*) — and notice that the answer starts with *тому що*, almost like an echo of the question.

**Зрозуміло is an answer, not an adjective.** It means "(it's) clear / got it" and stands on its own, just like English "Got it." The opposite: **Не зрозуміло**, or more often **Я не розумію** (I don't understand).

**Це and цей are not the same word.** *Це* stands alone: "this is". *Цей / ця / це / ці* attach to a noun and follow its gender: *цей стіл* (this table). ⚠️ The most common beginner mistake: saying *це стіл* when you mean "this table" — what the listener hears is "this is a table".

grammars.title: Three genders, and how to guess them from the ending
body: Cover the right-hand column, look at the ending, guess the gender. Once you can do this smoothly, half the work of Ukrainian grammar is done.
after: Only the last row has to be learned word by word. Luckily there aren't many words in **-ь** at A1, and most of them come up again and again in this course until their gender sticks on its own.

grammars.title: Це vs цей / ця / це / ці
body: *Це* introduces something. *Цей* points at something already in front of you. Compare the rows in pairs.
after: For neuter nouns both forms happen to be **це** — so *Це вікно маленьке* can mean "This is a small window" or "This window is small". Context decides, and Ukrainians are never confused by it.

blocks.text: Read the first column and guess the gender before you look at the third. These words come back over the next ten units, so time spent here pays off twice.

blocks.title: Words ending in -ь: the only ones to memorize
items: **Masculine:** день (day), тиждень (week), місяць (month), лікар (doctor — consonant), учитель (teacher), готель (hotel).
A handy mini-pattern: words ending in **-ість** and **-ощ** are almost always feminine; words ending in **-тель** and **-ар** are almost always masculine.
⚠️ Don't spend time memorizing this list now. Bookmark the page and come back when a word actually gets in your way.

exercises.prompt: What gender is each word? Write він, вона, or воно.
Fill in the blanks with цей, ця, or це.
Put the words in the right order.

answers: вона — він — воно — вона — він — воно
Що це? — Це не стіл. — Це шафа. — Це велике вікно. — Це легко.
Що це? — Це вікно. — Це не шафа. — Цей стіл великий. — Чому? Тому що шафа закінчується на -а.
